family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Return the uppercase initials of a full name, taking the first letter of each whitespace-separated word in order and joining them with no separator. Assume the name has at least one word.
hidden_tests: assert get_initials('a b c d e') == 'ABCDE'

reference:
def get_initials(name):
    return ''.join(w[0].upper() for w in name.split())

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a full name of one or more whitespace-separated words, if there is more than one word, move the last word to the front followed by a comma, keeping the remaining words in order; if there is only one word, return it unchanged.
visible_tests: assert reverse_name('Ada Marie Lovelace') == 'Lovelace, Ada Marie'
hidden_tests: assert reverse_name('Mary Jane Watson') == 'Watson, Mary Jane'
assert reverse_name('a b c d e') == 'e, a b c d'
assert reverse_name('Elon Reeve Musk') == 'Musk, Elon Reeve'
assert reverse_name('one two three') == 'three, one two'
assert reverse_name('Tim Berners Lee') == 'Lee, Tim Berners'
assert reverse_name('y z w') == 'w, y z'
reference:
def reverse_name(name):
    parts = name.split()
    if len(parts) == 1:
        return parts[0]
    last = parts[-1]
    rest = ' '.join(parts[:-1])
    return f"{last}, {rest}"

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Convert a string into a URL-friendly slug: lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that are not lowercase letters or digits with a single hyphen, and strip any leading or trailing hyphens.
reference:
def slugify(s):
    import re
    s = s.lower().strip()
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s)
    s = s.strip('-')
    s = re.sub(r'-{2,}', '-', s)
    return s

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Convert a string into a slug the same way as ordinary slugification but using underscores instead of hyphens as the separator: lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that are not lowercase letters or digits with a single underscore, and strip leading/trailing underscores.
reference:
def slug_with_underscore(s):
    import re
    s = s.lower().strip()
    s = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', s)
    s = s.strip('_')
    s = re.sub(r'_{2,}', '_', s)
    return s
